column1: # budgets.tsv -- M119a (#2485): the budget table. One row per corpus id
# (join corpus.tsv on `id`). A budget is a CONTRACT: the number the bench
# fails past, derived from a MEASURED baseline by the named margin --
# `budget = baseline x margin`, checked by tools/gate/bench-check.py.
# A row with no baseline, no margin, or no citation does not ship.
# Columns:
#   id        corpus row id (must exist in corpus.tsv)
#   cmp       `<=` (upper bound: latency, wall, buffered bytes) or
#             `>=` (lower bound: throughput)
#   budget    the contract number in the row's unit
#   baseline  the MEASURED value the budget is pinned from. Where the
#             instrument's resolution bounds the observation (e.g. a value
#             observed below one tick), the baseline is the resolution
#             floor, stated on the issue with the raw observation.

# margin the named headroom: `x`, `+|-

%`, or `+|-` (in unit)
#   ref       where the baseline run is recorded: `#<issue>`, `issue:<n>`,
#             or `gate:<id>` (+ optional `; <note>`)
# Baselines measured 2026-10-17 on the development host (Apple silicon,
# macOS 27.2, this branch's tree) and recorded on issue #2485. Two rows
# sit at their instrument's resolution floor: `sysinfo` uptime printed
# ticks=0 (the whole boot fits in the first 1 Hz tick; the runner's own
# marker wait observed ~1.0 s wall to 'kernel terminal state'), and the
# GOSH `time` builtin printed real=0.00s for both commands (centisecond
# resolution) -- both baselines are the floor, stated there.
# Margins re-pinned on #2486 (same host, same day): the first live-bench
# runs showed intra-host spread wider than the margins named from single
# samples -- hf-read 2799..8442 KiB/s across 8 same-shape boots (-67%),
# smp-scale-c1 72.0M..157.4M ticks (2.33x), smp-scale-c2 26.3M..82.8M
# (3.15x). The baselines stay (still the best-case observations); the
# margins now cover the observed spread: hf-read -75% (2799 min, budget
# 2110), c1/c2 x4. smp-scale-c4's observed max (51.7M, 1.55x) already
# fits its x2, unchanged.
# wm-present-latency re-pinned on #2490 (same host, 2026-10-20): #2729's
# per-report cv-input fan (a correctness fix -- the batched press landed
# off the drag rows) made burst input->present latency drain-bound:
# lat_max sat ~1.01s while the tick-sampled fan delivered at heartbeat
# cadence, and now rides the seat's event-queue drain behind merged
# heartbeats (~2.0s under the scripted 8-step burst). Bisected over 6
# commits -- 69de0d15/05835e7c/39fec697 lat_max ~= 1.01s, 7bdab656/HEAD
# ~= 2.0s; cadence row unmoved. New baseline is the best observed sample;
# the idle-queue interactive path fans immediately, so the bound being
# contracted remains the burst-absorption shape the leg measures.
# card #3042 (same host, 2026-10-22): hf-read re-pinned after card #3035
# raised the EL0 file-io cap 2048 B -> 32 KiB. The new baseline is the
# best observed sample at the new cap: 80,932 KiB/s from this card's K=3
# 36,834..67,815). The -75% margin is kept -- the pre-raise spread that
# earned it was ~3x intra-host, and both K=3 spreads at the new cap sit
# inside it.
# app-launch-cold / go-rss are new legs from this card (see corpus.tsv):
# the launch row is a 1 Hz floor-resolution bound like boot-shell's
# (observed 3 ticks incl. the runner's marker-forward settle), and go-rss
# is the resident-footprint contract the capacity table cites (GOCALC
# observed 5,984,260 B idled, post-#3032 demand-zero BSS).
# card #3040 (same host, 2026-10-22): the M170f pins.
# wm-present-latency re-measured on the post-#3034 tree: the WND.BIN
# burst's input->present worst-case dropped from ~2.0 s (the drain-bound
# shape of #2490) to 702,435 us on this card's live-wm-pacing run — the
# damage tick answers inside the burst now. Baseline is that measured
# value; the x2 margin family is kept.
# timer-jitter is the deadline overlay's own number (`timertest jitter 20`
# max_late_us): four same-shape boots observed 4,696 / 4,991 / 5,501 /
# 17,823 — the tail is the ~1 ms IRQ-side retry deferrals under
# sched_lock contention #3036 documented. Baseline is the best observed
# sample; the x5 margin covers the observed tail.
# seat-key-latency (new leg): three-Go-runtime seat (GOTABWM + GOCALC +
# GOSOUND PCM), keys over cv-input; K=3 samples 999,777 / 1,002,732 /
# 1,003,770 — ~1.0 s, i.e. still about one tick_avg on this shape.
# Baseline is the best observed sample; x2.
